study_identification_part.si_4_title: Lifespan Normative Modeling of Brain Microstructure

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study aggregates 19 public datasets for the reference normative model and 2 additional datasets for model adaptation. The 19 training/testing datasets are: ABCD, AOMIC, CAMCAN, CHBMP, CHCP, HCP-A, HCP-D, HCP-YA, PedsDTI (NIHPD), PING, PNC, QTAB, QTIM, SLIM, UKBB, ADNI3 (controls), HBN (controls), OASIS3 (controls), and PPMI (controls). The adaptation datasets are NIMHANS and UCLA.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: We pooled dMRI data from 19 public neuroimaging studies... We included the following public datasets... ABCD, AOMIC, CAMCAN, CHBMP, CHCP, HCP_A & HCP_D, HCP_YA, PedsDTI, PING, PNC, QTAB, QTIM, SLIM, and UKBB. Several clinical datasets were also included... ADNI3, OASIS3, PPMI, and HBN. Importantly, only the healthy controls (HC) of the latter four datasets were added to the pool of training data... Two additional datasets were used for the model adaptation experiments: NIMHANS and UCLA.

answer.ADNI-3: controls for training/testing; MCI and Dementia for clinical anomaly detection

answer.OASIS-3: controls for training/testing; MCI and Dementia for clinical anomaly detection

answer.NIMHANS: model adaptation and clinical anomaly detection (MCI, Dementia)

answer.UCLA: model adaptation and clinical anomaly detection (22qDel)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: 19 public datasets were used to build the reference normative model using an 80/20 train-test split (repeated 10 times). Clinical groups from ADNI3 and OASIS3 were used for initial anomaly detection. NIMHANS and UCLA datasets were used for model adaptation (50% HC for adaptation, 50% HC and patients for testing).
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Training and testing data sets were created with an 80% to 20% sample split... only the healthy controls (HC) of the latter four datasets [ADNI3, OASIS3, PPMI, HBN] were added to the pool of training data... the patients in ADNI3 and OASIS3 were included as test data for the anomaly detection experiment... Two additional datasets were used for the model adaptation experiments: NIMHANS and UCLA.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A total of 54,583 healthy individuals from 19 datasets remained for the reference model after quality control. The training set size was approximately 43,666 (80% split). Models were built for four DTI metrics (FA, MD, AD, RD) across 22 regions of interest.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: totaling N=54,583 individuals... a total of 54,583 subjects remained for training [reference population pool]... we ran HBR 10 times on each of the 80% sample splits (n=43,666).

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The overall age range is 4 to 91 years. The weighted mean (50.12) and pooled SD (6.96) were calculated based on the demographic data provided for the 19 training datasets in Table 2. Median age for the largest cohort (UK Biobank, N=36,864) is 64.6. The training phase demographics were not explicitly stated but are inferred to be similar due to random 80/20 splitting.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: covering almost the entire lifespan (totaling N=54,583 individuals; age: 4-91 years).

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex distribution for the overall reference cohort (N=54,583) was calculated from Table 2, resulting in 28,904 females (53.0%) and 25,679 males (47.0%). Training phase numbers are inferred based on the 80% split (43,666 total) assuming representative sampling.
